title: Improvise over a chord loop
summary: Make up a right-hand line over four bars of chords your left hand repeats again and again.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil

figure.alt: Four boxes stacked, standing for the four-bar chord loop the left hand repeats, a steady floor the right hand tries new ideas over, one loop at a time.

steps.title: Improvise over a chord loop
steps.body:
A chord loop is four bars of chords that repeat, which gives the right hand a safe, steady floor to try things on. Nothing you play with the right hand can break the loop, so this is the safest place to take a musical risk.

1. Play the four-bar chord loop with the left hand until it repeats on its own, without you thinking about it.
2. With the right hand, try single notes from the chords underneath, one loop at a time, changing something new each loop.
3. Try one rhythm idea across a whole loop: all long, slow notes, then a loop of short, quick ones.
4. Once you find a loop you like, record it before it is forgotten.

Improvising is not about having no rules. The chord loop is the rule, and everything interesting happens inside it.

figure.alt: The same four-bar loop, played steady with the left hand alone first, then with a new right-hand idea tried over it each time it repeats.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: the chord loop alone with the left hand, until it is steady
Sitting 2: right-hand ideas over the loop, changing something new each loop
Sitting 3: try the loop with all long notes, then all short notes
Sitting 4: play your favourite version of the loop, then once as if recording
An old piece played once, for a change of pace

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Play the chord loop alone once, then play your favourite improvised version over it, hands in the frame.
